**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The MINCOMMIT rule is satisfied here. Key points:

- **No take-or-pay on us.** There is no minimum purchase commitment, shortfall fee, or volume cap on PB anywhere in the agreement. The committed spend runs the other direction: SFJ commits to fund up to $120M of Development Costs (Sections 4.1–4.2), which the rule expressly treats as acceptable ("Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine").
- **Our payments are contingent and trued up.** Approval Payments under Article 6 only arise if Regulatory Approval is obtained, and Section 6.2 scales them pro rata to actual Development Costs funded, with express "true-up payments" — the true-up-not-penalty structure the playbook wants.
- **Exits exist.** Buy-out options (Sections 6.7.1–6.7.2) and at-will termination (Section 14.2.2), so this is nowhere near the walk-away scenario of a multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right.

Noted in the rationale but deliberately not flagged: the $110M floor on the Elected Total Amount (a minimum draw of funding we *receive*, with consideration trued up under 6.2), the matched-spend/use-of-proceeds covenant in Section 4.2.3, and the 300% exit payment on at-will termination — the last being termination economics that belongs to the termination rule rather than being double-flagged here.
